title: Dasakam 11
description: The four sages visit Vaikuntha; Jaya and Vijaya are cursed, then born as Hiranyaksha and Hiranyakashipu.

stanzas.sanskrit:
क्रमेण सर्गे परिवर्धमाने कदापि दिव्याः सनकादयस्ते ।
भवद्विलोकाय विकुण्ठलोकं प्रपेदिरे मारुतमन्दिरेश ॥ ११-१॥
stanzas.commentary_en: As creation progressed, the divine sages Sanaka and the others wanting to pay their respects to Bhagwan moved on the way to Vaikunta loka.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
krameṇa sarge parivardhamāne
kadāpi divyāḥ sanakādayaste |
bhavadvilokāya vikuṇṭhalokaṃ
prapedire mārutamandireśa || 11-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
मनोज्ञनैश्रेयसकाननाद्यैरनेकवापीमणिमन्दिरैश्च ।
अनोपमं तं भवतो निकेतं मुनीश्वराः प्रापुरतीतकक्ष्याः ॥ ११-२॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Crossing six fortresses and a beautiful garden full of Kalpa trees, known as "NAISREYAM", surrounded by several lakes and mansions shining with pearls and gems, the divine sages came to the abode of Bhagwan.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
manojñanaiḥśreyasa kānanādyai-
-ranekavāpīmaṇimandiraiśca |
anopamaṃ taṃ bhavato niketaṃ
munīśvarāḥ prāpuratītakakṣyāḥ || 11-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
भवद्दिदृक्षून्भवनं विविक्षून्द्वाःस्थौ जयस्तान् विजयोऽप्यरुन्धाम् ।
तेषां च चित्ते पदमाप कोपः सर्वं भवत्प्रेरणयैव भूमन् ॥ ११-३॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The sages were about to enter Bhagwan’s abode, when two gatekeepers, Jaya and Vijaya stopped them. This made the sages angry. All this happened by Bhagwan prompting only.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
bhavaddidṛkṣūn bhavanaṃ vivikṣūn
dvāḥsthau jayastān vijayo’pyarundhām |
teṣāṃ ca citte padamāpa kopaḥ
sarvaṃ bhavatpreraṇayaiva bhūman || 11-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
वैकुण्ठलोकानुचितप्रचेष्टौ कष्टौ युवां दैत्यगतिं भजेतम् ।
इति प्रशप्तौ भवदाश्रयौ तौ हरिस्मृतिर्नोऽस्त्विति नेमतुस्तान् ॥ ११-४॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The Sages cursed Jaya and Vijaya to become asuras, as the conduct of the two made them unfit to be in Vaikunta. Jaya and Vijaya requested the sages to pardon them for their mistake.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
vaikuṇṭhalokānucitapraceṣṭau
kaṣṭau yuvāṃ daityagatiṃ bhajetam |
iti praśaptau bhavadāśrayau tau
harismṛtirno’stviti nematustān || 11-4 ||

stanzas.commentary_en: Knowing all what had happened, Bhagwan came out along with Lakshmi, with HIS charming arm resting on Garuda. The sages were delighted to see Bhagwan’s beautiful form.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tadetadājñāya bhavānavāptaḥ
sahaiva lakṣmyā bahirambujākṣa |
khageśvarāṃsārpitacārubāhu-
-rānandayaṃstānabhirāmamūrtyā || 11-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
प्रसाद्य गीर्भिः स्तुवतो मुनीन्द्राननन्यनाथावथ पार्षदौ तौ ।
संरम्भयोगेन भवैस्त्रिभिर्मामुपेतमित्यात्तकृपं न्यगादीः ॥ ११-६॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Jaya and Vijaya, now took refuge at Bhagwan’s feet, prostrated and asked for pardon. Bhagwan with great kindness said that Jaya and Vijaya will have only three births in earth as asuras and then will come back to Vaikunta.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
prasādya gīrbhiḥ stuvato munīndrā-
-nananyanāthāvatha pārṣadau tau |
saṃrambhayogena bhavaistribhirmā-
-mupetamityāttakṛpaṃ nyagādīḥ || 11-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्वदीयभृत्यावथ काश्यपात्तौ सुरारिवीरावुदितौ दितौ द्वौ ।
सन्ध्यासमुत्पादनकष्टचेष्टौ यमौ च लोकस्य यमाविवान्यौ ॥ ११-७॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Then, Bhagwan’s two attendants took birth as great Asuras through Diti and her husband sage Kashyapa. Both were cruel in nature due to mother Diti conceiving them at the wrong time of twilight.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tvadīyabhṛtyāvatha kāśyapāt tau
surārivīrāvuditau ditau dvau |
sandhyāsamutpādanakaṣṭaceṣṭau
yamau ca lokasya yamāvivānyau || 11-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
हिरण्यपूर्वः कशिपुः किलैकः परो हिरण्याक्ष इति प्रतीतः ।
उभौ भवन्नाथमशेषलोकं रुषा न्यरुन्धां निजवासनान्धौ ॥ ११-८॥
stanzas.commentary_en: One son was known by the name of Hiranyakashipu and the other was known as Hiranyaaksha. The two brothers tormented the whole world with their evil tendencies.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
hiraṇyapūrvaḥ kaśipuḥ kilaikaḥ
paro hiraṇyākṣa iti pratītaḥ |
ubhau bhavannāthamaśeṣalokaṃ
ruṣā nyarundhāṃ nijavāsanāndhau || 11-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
तयोर्हिरण्याक्षमहासुरेन्द्रो रणाय धावन्ननवाप्तवैरी ।
भवत्प्रियां क्ष्मां सलिले निमज्य चचार गर्वाद्विनदन् गदावान् ॥ ११-९॥
stanzas.commentary_en: One of them, Hiranyaksha sought an opponent to fight. Since no one was ready to fight with him, he immersed the earth in the waters and roamed around the worlds with his mace.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tayorhiraṇyākṣamahāsurendro
raṇāya dhāvannanavāptavairī |
bhavatpriyāṃ kṣmāṃ salile nimajya
cacāra garvādvinadan gadāvān || 11-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
ततो जलेशात्सदृशं भवन्तं निशम्य बभ्राम गवेषयंस्त्वाम् ।
भक्तैकदृश्यः स कृपानिधे त्वं निरुन्धि रोगान् मरुदालयेश ॥ ११-१०॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
God Varuna, the Lord of waters told Hiranyaksha that only Lord Vishnu is proper opponent for him. He then went around searching for Lord Vishnu, who can be attained only by his devotees.
Bhattathiri requested Bhagwan whose form is visible only to his true devotees, to cure him of his ailments.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tato jaleśāt sadṛśaṃ bhavantaṃ
niśamya babhrāma gaveṣayaṃstvām |
bhaktaikadṛśyaḥ sa kṛpānidhe tvaṃ
nirundhi rogān marudālayeśa || 11-10 ||
